title: Apache Kafka

spark.tagline: Understand append-only partitioned logs, consumer group rebalancing, ISR replication, and exactly-once semantics from first principles.
spark.takeaway: Kafka is a durable, partitioned commit log—not an ephemeral in-memory queue. Throughput comes from sequential disk I/O and zero-copy sendfile().
spark.summary: Understand append-only partitioned logs, consumer group rebalancing, ISR replication, and exactly-once semantics from first principles.
spark.byteSummary:
Understand append-only partitioned logs, consumer group rebalancing, ISR replication, and exactly-once semantics from first principles.

A Kafka topic is split into ordered, immutable partitions. Producers append records to the tail of a partition, and consumers track their own integer offset.

Mastering Kafka means reasoning about partition parallelism, acks=all durability, consumer lag, and poison-pill dead-letter isolation.

learningJourney.title: Topics, partitions, and sequential disk I/O
learningJourney.explanation: A Kafka topic is split into ordered, immutable partitions. Producers append records to the tail of a partition, and consumers track their own integer offset.

ideas.title: Ordering guarantee
ideas.description: Kafka guarantees strict message ordering only within a single partition—never across partitions of the same topic.

ideas.title: Zero-copy delivery
ideas.description: Brokers transfer segment files directly from OS page cache to the network NIC via `sendfile()`, bypassing user-space copies.

learningJourney.title: Consumer groups & offset management
learningJourney.explanation: Within a consumer group, each partition is assigned to at most one consumer instance. Max parallelism equals the partition count.

learningJourney.title: ISR replication, rebalancing & DLQ patterns
learningJourney.explanation: Explore how Kafka maintains In-Sync Replicas (ISR), handles cooperative sticky rebalancing, and isolates poison-pill messages.

tabbedExplorer.name: ISR Replication
tabbedExplorer.title: In-Sync Replicas & High Watermark
tabbedExplorer.desc: Consumers can only read up to the High Watermark (HW)—the highest offset replicated to all In-Sync Replicas.
tabbedExplorer.rule: Never set unclean.leader.election.enable=true on financial or state-critical topics.

tabbedExplorer.name: Cooperative Rebalance
tabbedExplorer.title: Incremental Cooperative Sticky Assignor
tabbedExplorer.desc: Only partitions that actually move between consumers are revoked, avoiding cluster-wide stop-the-world pauses.
tabbedExplorer.rule: Offload slow external HTTP/DB calls or bound max.poll.interval.ms to avoid spurious rebalances.
tabbedExplorer.use: Large consumer groups (>50 instances) scaling dynamically.

learningJourney.title: Consumer lag, hot partitions & exactly-once myths
learningJourney.explanation: At-least-once delivery + idempotent consumers is almost always cleaner and cheaper than cross-system distributed transactions.

qaDetails.summary: How do you fix a hot partition caused by a celebrity tenant key?
qaDetails.body: Salt the partition key (e.g., `tenantId + '#' + (hash % 8)`) when strict per-tenant total order is not required, or isolate VIP tenants to dedicated partitions.

qaDetails.summary: Why does Kafka's 'Exactly-Once Semantics (EOS)' not cover external DB writes?
qaDetails.body: Kafka transactions only span Kafka topics (consume-transform-produce). Writing to Postgres still requires an idempotency key / upsert or Transactional Outbox.

knowledgeCheck.question: A topic has 6 partitions and a consumer group has 10 running consumer instances. How many instances sit idle?

options.text: A. 0 instances — Kafka splits partitions dynamically
options.feedback: A single partition cannot be consumed by two instances in the same consumer group.
Correct! At most 6 instances can hold 1 partition each; the extra 4 remain idle standbys.
6 instances are active (one per partition), leaving 4 idle.

tipsAndTricks: Partition count sets the upper bound on consumer-group parallelism—increasing partitions later changes key-to-partition hash mapping.
Never block the Kafka poll() loop with unbounded synchronous RPCs; if poll() exceeds max.poll.interval.ms, the broker kicks the consumer out and triggers a rebalance.
Prefer At-Least-Once + Idempotent Consumer (dedup key in DB/Redis) over Kafka EOS when writing to external datastores.
finalSummaryEyebrow: The idea to keep with you
finalSummaryTitle: Partition by key for order. Replicate with min.insync.replicas. Make consumers idempotent.
finalSummary: Mastering Kafka means reasoning about partition parallelism, acks=all durability, consumer lag, and poison-pill dead-letter isolation.
